I have been farming these lands in Quzhou for over 30 years. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land, and I know every piece of it. I went to middle school — enough to read seed labels and follow the agricultural station's guidance, but I don't fuss with too many new ideas. I stick with what works.

The wheat went into the ground last October, same as every year. I used an improved variety — something like the ones from the seed station, reliable for this area. I rotary-tilled before sowing and put down compound fertilizer as basal. Right now it's April, the wheat is coming back green strong. I will top-dress with urea at jointing, irrigate four times total (returning green, jointing, heading, and grain filling), and spray about four times for weeds, aphids, and rust. I expect around 1,050 jin per mu — not the highest, but steady.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize. No time to plough — I will no-till drill the hybrid maize seed straight into the wheat stubble. That saves time and keeps moisture. I'll apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea when the maize is knee-high. I'll irrigate three times and spray three times — mainly herbicide and corn borer control. I target about 1,100 jin per mu for the maize.

I don't grow cotton anymore. It pays okay some years, but the labor is too much for me now — too many pesticide sprays, and my back isn't what it was. The wheat-maize double crop is simpler, the machinery is easy to hire, and I can sell both to the same buyers. My son works in Handan city, so I manage most of this myself with some hired labor at harvest. This is the system I trust.
